title: Callas Forever
full_review:
Here is a fabricated but true-in-spirit story of self-obsessed opera diva Maria Callas' lonely last years in Paris, after losing both her voice and her longtime amour, Aristotle Onassis.

Eschewing a traditional biographical format, "Callas Forever" (Regent Releasing) concerns the efforts of her (fictitious) manager (Jeremy Irons) -- now a rock promoter having an affair with a male artist who worships Callas' voice -- to persuade the diva that she can have a second career by making film versions of her most notable operas in which she will lip-sync to her old recordings.

French accent notwithstanding, Fanny Ardant -- who played Callas onstage in the play "Master Class" -- succeeds to a remarkable degree in capturing the Greek-American soprano's temperament and physical appearance.

Director Franco Zeffirelli -- in real life, a close friend and colleague of Callas -- directs with the authority you'd expect and, no stranger to filmed operas (his "La Traviata" and "Otello" movies were vividly cinematic), brings special flair to the "Carmen" sequences within this film.

Still, this is specialized material that will be of most interest to Callas fans and opera buffs.

Joan Plowright excels in the role of a journalist friend of Callas, who helps the Irons character pull Callas out of her depressed state.

Because of a few instances of rough and crude language and a couple of mild sexual situations, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. Not rated by the Motion Picture Association of America.
